title: new16; unfixed in every release
live_proof: inspection in the 3.22.0 tree: nodeWrite() inserts the node into the hash with no check for iNode==0, while nodeHashDelete() keys off iNode and treats 0 as 'not in the hash', so nodeRelease() frees a block that stays linked in aHash[0]. Fixed upstream in d21bd37c7c; the note recorded with the entry is that it is unfixed in every release up to the one we checked
object: an RtreeNode linked into aHash[0] while still carrying iNode==0
lifetime_ender: nodeRelease() frees the block, but nodeHashDelete() cannot unlink it because it keys off an iNode of 0
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator, with an unusual precondition that is part of the defect rather than an artifact: the %_node INSERT must be suppressed by a BEFORE INSERT trigger raising IGNORE, and no other rowid insert may have happened on the connection, so that last_insert_rowid() returns 0
